messages:
sarah_support: FYI customer ACME reported an invoice showing ~240 reserved GPU hours for their dedicated pool last month but our dashboard shows ~35h and token burn was low. They want an explanation + SLA credit. :eyes:
kevin_billing: Can you drop the account and pool IDs? I’ll pull ledger lines and invoice items.
sarah_support: acct=acme-corp, pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-73. Invoice 2026-02-28. I already flagged billing but they pushed to support for faster turnaround.
maria_engineering: A couple quick hypotheses: 1) prewarm/warmup probes attributed to the pool (headroom probes) 2) VM/GPU warm-up instances counted as reserved hours due to a stale lifecycle tag 3) cross-pool failover routing that briefly charged another pool but invoice attribution went to this pool.
nash: ops-bot just posted a recent deploy around that time, might be related. ops-bot: deploy finished: release/3.12.1 - canary -> prod at 2026-02-14T03:12Z (note: no consumer traffic)
nash: whoops wrong name — meant ashwin_sre: Can we get the instance lifecycle/events log for pool dedicated-eu-west-2-73 between 2026-02-01 and 2026-02-28? Also check warmup_probe_count metric and prewarm probe headers.
sarah_support: pulling logs now, attaching snippets: ```
[2026-02-12T00:05:12Z] pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-73 instance=i-0a1b2c3d status=prewarm probe_id=pm-99
[2026-02-12T00:05:15Z] pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-73 instance=i-0a1b2c3d billing=reserved hours=0.5
[2026-02-12T00:06:01Z] routing=failover src_pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-12 dst_pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-73 reason=capacity_shortfall
```
kevin_billing: Hmm the ledger shows a block of hourly charges on 2026-02-12-14:00 -> 2026-02-13-06:00 totalling ~200h across that window for that account. Need to see reconciliation between instance-up events and ledger lines. If prewarm probes are billed as reserved, that could explain a big chunk.
maria_engineering: Also check whether the prewarm probe requests included the X-Redwood-Routing header. If header missing, they can be attributed to default pool mapping which sometimes pins to the committed pool. There was a routing fallback change in 3.12.1 that strips headers for synthetic probes — might be the culprit.
nash: ashwin_sre here — reproduced locally: when a probe is retried in a tight loop and the instance stays warm, our metering service emits an hourly allocation every time the lifecycle flips even if tokens=0. Repro steps I used: ```
# simulate probe retries
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "X-Redwood-Probe: true" -H "X-Redwood-Routing: pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-73" https://internal-probe.redwood/health; done
# then check meter events
curl -s "https://internal-metering.redwood/api/v1/events?instance=i-0a1b2c3d&from=2026-02-12T00:00Z&to=2026-02-13T00:00Z" | jq . | less
```
sarah_support: Good repro. Customer says they had a bot that hammered keepalive endpoints during their migration window — matches the retry pattern.
kevin_billing: Recommend we patch metering to dedupe lifecycle flips within a short window and mark those as non-billable if tokens==0 and probe header present. For immediate customer remediation: 1) audit ledger and produce an invoice adjustment proposal 2) apply provisional SLA credit while we investigate and 3) offer configuration to exempt probe traffic.
maria_engineering: I can open a PR for a hotfix — short-term guard: ignore lifecycle transitions when header X-Redwood-Probe=true OR when token_delta==0. Long term: change attribution logic to prefer explicit routing header.
nash: ashwin_sre: I’ll run a backfill to mark events from 2026-02-12 with probe header as non-billable and send delta CSV to billing. Will need billing sign-off before applying credits.
kevin_billing: Please include ledger ids and invoice item ids in the CSV. I’ll queue a one-off invoice adjustment and request SLA credit approval.
sarah_support: I notified the customer that we have a remediation plan and that we’re preparing a provisional credit; they asked for ETA.
maria_engineering: Hotfix PR target in next 6 hours, backfill script within 12. I’ll post links when created. :white_check_mark:
kevin_billing: Thanks all — once we have the CSV and PR link I’ll escalate to finance for the credit and let the customer know expected timeline.
ops-bot: ticket created: #SUP-2026-1129 (dedicated-hours-divergence). status=investigating
sarah_support: closing loop: customer replied :thumbsup: wants regular updates. I’ll keep thread updated as we finish the backfill and credit.
